# Diagnosing Intermittent Starting Issues on a 2007 Citroen C4

When a 2007 Citroen C4 2LR diesel refuses to crank but delivers a distinct click, you are looking at a classic electrical architecture failure mode. The fact that the battery holds charge and jump-starting the vehicle works immediately rules out simple depletion or poor grounding at the main negative terminal. If the engine turns over instantly with an external power source, the starter motor itself is mechanically sound, and the primary ignition circuit has sufficient voltage to engage the solenoid. The problem lies in the reliability of the vehicle's internal switching logic or its ability to maintain a stable ground path under load.

In modern automotive ECUs, the "click" you hear is the solenoid engaging, but the starter motor isn't receiving the full current required to spin the crankshaft. This specific behavior often points to a high-resistance connection within the main power delivery chain or a failing ignition switch contact point. Unlike software bugs where logic fails silently, mechanical-electrical interfaces in diesel vehicles like the 2LR are notoriously sensitive to voltage drops exceeding 0.1 volts during the cranking phase.

One of the most common culprits for this specific symptom is the condition of the main battery ground strap or the chassis earth points near the engine block. Over time, the anti-corrosion grease on these terminals can dry out and flake off, creating a thin insulating layer that looks clean to the eye but introduces significant resistance. When you jump-start the car, the heavy-gauge cables bypass these corroded factory terminals entirely, providing a low-resistance path directly from the battery to the starter solenoid. This is why the issue resolves immediately with external leads; the internal connection point is effectively being shorted out by the jumper cables.

To troubleshoot this without visiting a garage that may not replicate the intermittent nature of the fault, start by inspecting the negative terminal block on the engine side. Look for any white crystalline deposits or green corrosion. Cleaning these points with an abrasive wire brush and applying fresh dielectric grease is often more effective than simply tightening the bolt if the threads are stripped or the pad is thin. Another critical check involves the starter earth point located on the transmission bell housing or directly on the engine block, depending on the specific chassis configuration of the C4. These points often accumulate oil and carbon deposits from exhaust leaks, which act as resistors when the voltage demand spikes during cranking.

Software-wise, while less common in mechanical failures, it is worth considering the immobilizer system if the dashboard indicator lights behave erratically. However, given that the engine starts perfectly with a jump, an immobilizer lockout is unlikely. The issue is almost certainly physical resistance in the power loop. If cleaning the terminals and earth points does not resolve the intermittent clicking, the starter solenoid itself may be failing to maintain contact under its own internal load, even though it engages when voltage is forced upon it from an external source.

For vehicle owners managing this specific model, carrying a jump starter is a valid short-term mitigation strategy, but addressing the high-resistance grounds will restore the reliability of the ignition system without needing to rely on external power sources every couple of months.
